results.description:
Version 11.3.1

Publication date: April 30th, 2024

Coordinate reference system: WGS 1984

Generalization: 99.5%

Scale: 1/1,000,000


The Office of the Geographer and Global Issues (GGI) at the U.S. Department of State produces the Large-Scale International Boundaries (LSIB) dataset. LSIB version 11.3.1, released April 30, 2024 is the current version of the dataset. The LSIB is the official international boundaries dataset of the U.S. government, and is recognized as a National Geospatial Data Asset and a core dataset in the US National Spatial Data Infrastructure. The LSIB is available for public download on geodata.state.gov, data.gov, and geoplatform.gov. To assist in GIS analysis and cartographic visualization, the Office of the Geographer and Global Issues also creates polygon datasets that incorporate the boundary alignment from the LSIB.

World Polygons Version 11.3.1 is a new collection of polygon datasets that is specifically designed to match the LSIB 11.3.1 dataset. The purpose of the World Polygons dataset is to enable geographic visualization, at multiple cartographic scales, which incorporates U.S. Government official international boundary alignment, cartographic styling that reflects the political status of boundaries, and country or area names used by the Department of State and other international standards. This dataset also provides a mechanism for attribute joins for the analysis and visualization of country-level information (e.g., gross domestic product or population of each country). To facilitate this effort, the dataset contains contain a series of spatial files in both shapefile (.shp), geopackage (.gpkg) and geodatabase (.gdb) formats, as well as Web Map Service (WMS) layers and accompanying attribute data (described below.:

Generalized lines were processed using tools from Mapshaper.org, specifically the Visvalingram-Wyatt generalization algorithm. The generalized polygon files have 65% or 99.5% of the original nodes removed from the high-resolution files. All datasets contain the same number of political entities. The styling guidance for the generalized files is the same as for the full-resolution polygons. As a general scale recommendation, the 99.5% generalized layers are suitable for use from global scales to 1:20 million, the 65% generalized layers from 1:20 million to 1:2 million, and the high-resolution layers from 1:2 million to 1:1. WMS service endpoints will be referenced via the online metadata page located athttps://geodata.state.gov

This is a beta release designed for testing and evaluation. Given the iterative nature of this effort, users should expect that subsequent releases will have modifications, including international land boundary alignment, shoreline resolution, attribute structure, and release formats.

The polygons are not a standalone dataset. They must be used with the matching LSIB overlay and a shoreline dataset. This polygon data set alone should not be relied upon as a representation of the views of the United States regarding sovereignty or international boundaries. The source LSIB line dataset is available for download on geodata.state.gov, data.gov, and geoplatform.gov. The inclusion of a shoreline file is intended only for cartographic purposes.


Cartographic Visualization

The proper use of the World Polygon dataset in cartographic products requires the layering of the LSIB lines on top of the polygons along with the corresponding shoreline dataset. The edges of the polygon must be turned off. When combined with the polygon dataset, the LSIB lines must be symbolized with a visual hierarchy corresponding with the “Rank” field and labeled according to the “Label” field. The polygons should not have an outline or stroke added that conflicts with the LSIB line depiction.

When using colors to separate geographic entities, use the “MapTint_2” or “Map_Sov_Tint_3” fields. These fields are populated with the GENC two- and three-character codes corresponding with the country or area that should be used to show sovereignty for cartographic purposes. In other words, these attributes link dependencies (e.g., Greenland) with the parent country (e.g., Denmark). Similar linkages are encoded in the WP_ID and WP_PAR_ID fields.

The “Label” field contains suggested labels for polygon entities. Not all polygons have required labels, and some labels are not suitable for use at all scales. The “Entity” field is not appropriate for labeling as that field is only designed for data management purposes and provides a readable name corresponding to a “WP_ID” entry. Labels derived from this field require additional manual editing. Any labels applied on cartographic products should be reviewed for appropriate use of diacritics, case, and should reflect general USG standards for the labeling of dependencies, areas of special sovereignty, and administrative units.

The polygon layers contain the Caspian Sea as a data artifact. The Caspian Sea does not need to be cartographically represented.

Additional information
Specific cartographic information can be found in Guidance Bulletins published by the Office of the Geographer and Global Issues (https://hiu.state.gov/data/cartographic_guidance_bulletins/).
For U.S. Government and military users, additional boundaries information and analysis can be accessed through the Boundaries and Sovereignty Encyclopedia (BASE) web application maintained by the Office of the Geographer and Global Issues. BASE can be accessed on the internet athttps://statetoday.net/base. Access requires a username and password which can be requested through the site for users with a .gov or .mil email address.

Overview

The Office of the Geographer and Global Issues at the U.S. Department of State produces the Large Scale International Boundaries (LSIB) dataset. The current edition is version 11.3 (published 19 December 2023). The 11.3 release contains updates to boundary lines and data refinements enabling reuse of the dataset. These data and generalized derivatives are the only international boundary lines approved for U.S. Government use. The contents of this dataset reflect U.S. Government policy on international boundary alignment, political recognition, and dispute status. They do not necessarily reflect de facto limits of control.


National Geospatial Data Asset

This dataset is a National Geospatial Data Asset managed by the Department of State on behalf of the Federal Geographic Data Committee's International Boundaries Theme.


Details

Sources for these data include treaties, relevant maps, and data from boundary commissions and national mapping agencies. Where available, the dataset incorporates information from courts, tribunals, and international arbitrations. The research and recovery of the data involves analysis of satellite imagery and elevation data. Due to the limitations of source materials and processing techniques, most lines are within 100 meters of their true position on the ground. 

Attributes

The dataset uses the following attributes:

Attribute Name

Explanation

Country Code

Country-level codes are from the Geopolitical Entities, Names, and Codes Standard (GENC). The Q2 code denotes a line representing a boundary associated with an area not in GENC.

Country Names

Names approved by the U.S. Board on Geographic Names (BGN). Names for lines associated with a Q2 code are descriptive and are not necessarily BGN-approved.

Label

Required text label for the line segment where scale permits

Rank/Status

Rank 1: International Boundary

Rank 2: Other Line of International Separation

Rank 3: Special Line

Notes

Explanation of any applicable special circumstances


Cartographic Usage

Depiction of the LSIB requires a visual differentiation between the three categories of boundaries: International Boundaries (Rank 1), Other Lines of International Separation (Rank 2), and Special Lines (Rank 3). Rank 1 lines must be the most visually prominent. Rank 2 lines must be less visually prominent than Rank 1 lines. Rank 3 lines must be shown in a manner visually subordinate to Ranks 1 and 2. Where scale permits, Rank 2 and 3 lines must be labeled in accordance with the “Label” field. Data marked with a Rank 2 or 3 designation does not necessarily correspond to a disputed boundary.

Additional cartographic information can be found in Guidance Bulletins published by the Office of the Geographer and Global Issues.

Additional Information

Analysis: For US government and military users, additional boundaries information and analysis can be accessed through the Boundaries and Sovereignty Encyclopedia (BASE) web application maintained by the Office of the Geographer and Global Issues. BASE can be accessed on the internet at https://statetoday.net/base . Access requires a username and password which can be requested through the site for users with a .gov or .mil email address.

Direct inquiries to internationalboundaries@state.gov.

Credits

The lines in the LSIB dataset are the product of decades of collaboration between geographers at the Department of State and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency with contributions from the Central Intelligence Agency and the UK Defence Geographic Centre. 

Attribution is welcome: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Geographer and Global Issues.

results.description:
Version 11.3.1

Publication date: April 30th, 2024

Coordinate reference system: WGS 1984

Generalization: 99.5%

Scale: 1/1,000,000

 

 

The Office of the Geographer and Global Issues (GGI) at the U.S. Department of State produces the Large-Scale International Boundaries (LSIB) dataset. LSIB version 11.3.1, released April 30, 2024 is the current version of the dataset. The LSIB is the official international boundaries dataset of the U.S. government, and is recognized as a National Geospatial Data Asset and a core dataset in the US National Spatial Data Infrastructure. The LSIB is available for public download on geodata.state.gov, data.gov, and geoplatform.gov. To assist in GIS analysis and cartographic visualization, the Office of the Geographer and Global Issues also creates polygon datasets that incorporate the boundary alignment from the LSIB.

World Polygons Version 11.3.1 is a new collection of polygon datasets that is specifically designed to match the LSIB 11.3.1 dataset. The purpose of the World Polygons dataset is to enable geographic visualization, at multiple cartographic scales, which incorporates U.S. Government official international boundary alignment, cartographic styling that reflects the political status of boundaries, and country or area names used by the Department of State and other international standards. This dataset also provides a mechanism for attribute joins for the analysis and visualization of country-level information (e.g., gross domestic product or population of each country). To facilitate this effort, the dataset contains contain a series of spatial files in both shapefile (.shp), geopackage (.gpkg) and geodatabase (.gdb) formats, as well as Web Map Service (WMS) layers and accompanying attribute data (described below.:

Generalized lines were processed using tools from Mapshaper.org, specifically the Visvalingram-Wyatt generalization algorithm. The generalized polygon files have 65% or 99.5% of the original nodes removed from the high-resolution files. All datasets contain the same number of political entities. The styling guidance for the generalized files is the same as for the full-resolution polygons. As a general scale recommendation, the 99.5% generalized layers are suitable for use from global scales to 1:20 million, the 65% generalized layers from 1:20 million to 1:2 million, and the high-resolution layers from 1:2 million to 1:1. WMS service endpoints will be referenced via the online metadata page located athttps://geodata.state.gov

This is a beta release designed for testing and evaluation. Given the iterative nature of this effort, users should expect that subsequent releases will have modifications, including international land boundary alignment, shoreline resolution, attribute structure, and release formats.

The polygons are not a standalone dataset. They must be used with the matching LSIB overlay and a shoreline dataset. This polygon data set alone should not be relied upon as a representation of the views of the United States regarding sovereignty or international boundaries. The source LSIB line dataset is available for download on geodata.state.gov, data.gov, and geoplatform.gov. The inclusion of a shoreline file is intended only for cartographic purposes.


Cartographic Visualization

The proper use of the World Polygon dataset in cartographic products requires the layering of the LSIB lines on top of the polygons along with the corresponding shoreline dataset. The edges of the polygon must be turned off. When combined with the polygon dataset, the LSIB lines must be symbolized with a visual hierarchy corresponding with the “Rank” field and labeled according to the “Label” field. The polygons should not have an outline or stroke added that conflicts with the LSIB line depiction.

When using colors to separate geographic entities, use the “MapTint_2” or “Map_Sov_Tint_3” fields. These fields are populated with the GENC two- and three-character codes corresponding with the country or area that should be used to show sovereignty for cartographic purposes. In other words, these attributes link dependencies (e.g., Greenland) with the parent country (e.g., Denmark). Similar linkages are encoded in the WP_ID and WP_PAR_ID fields.

The “Label” field contains suggested labels for polygon entities. Not all polygons have required labels, and some labels are not suitable for use at all scales. The “Entity” field is not appropriate for labeling as that field is only designed for data management purposes and provides a readable name corresponding to a “WP_ID” entry. Labels derived from this field require additional manual editing. Any labels applied on cartographic products should be reviewed for appropriate use of diacritics, case, and should reflect general USG standards for the labeling of dependencies, areas of special sovereignty, and administrative units.

The polygon layers contain the Caspian Sea as a data artifact. The Caspian Sea does not need to be cartographically represented.

 

Additional information
Specific cartographic information can be found in Guidance Bulletins published by the Office of the Geographer and Global Issues (https://hiu.state.gov/data/cartographic_guidance_bulletins/).
For U.S. Government and military users, additional boundaries information and analysis can be accessed through the Boundaries and Sovereignty Encyclopedia (BASE) web application maintained by the Office of the Geographer and Global Issues. BASE can be accessed on the internet athttps://statetoday.net/base. Access requires a username and password which can be requested through the site for users with a .gov or .mil email address.

results.title: DoS_WP_11_3_1_Shoreline_G99_5
results.description:
Version 11.3.1

Publication date: April 30th, 2024

Coordinate reference system: WGS 1984

Generalization: 99.5%

Scale: 1/1,000,000

 

 

The Office of the Geographer and Global Issues (GGI) at the U.S. Department of State produces the Large-Scale International Boundaries (LSIB) dataset. LSIB version 11.3.1, released April 30, 2024 is the current version of the dataset. The LSIB is the official international boundaries dataset of the U.S. government, and is recognized as a National Geospatial Data Asset and a core dataset in the US National Spatial Data Infrastructure. The LSIB is available for public download on geodata.state.gov, data.gov, and geoplatform.gov. To assist in GIS analysis and cartographic visualization, the Office of the Geographer and Global Issues also creates polygon datasets that incorporate the boundary alignment from the LSIB.

World Polygons Version 11.3.1 is a new collection of polygon datasets that is specifically designed to match the LSIB 11.3.1 dataset. The purpose of the World Polygons dataset is to enable geographic visualization, at multiple cartographic scales, which incorporates U.S. Government official international boundary alignment, cartographic styling that reflects the political status of boundaries, and country or area names used by the Department of State and other international standards. This dataset also provides a mechanism for attribute joins for the analysis and visualization of country-level information (e.g., gross domestic product or population of each country). To facilitate this effort, the dataset contains contain a series of spatial files in both shapefile (.shp), geopackage (.gpkg) and geodatabase (.gdb) formats, as well as Web Map Service (WMS) layers and accompanying attribute data (described below.:

Generalized lines were processed using tools from Mapshaper.org, specifically the Visvalingram-Wyatt generalization algorithm. The generalized polygon files have 65% or 99.5% of the original nodes removed from the high-resolution files. All datasets contain the same number of political entities. The styling guidance for the generalized files is the same as for the full-resolution polygons. As a general scale recommendation, the 99.5% generalized layers are suitable for use from global scales to 1:20 million, the 65% generalized layers from 1:20 million to 1:2 million, and the high-resolution layers from 1:2 million to 1:1. WMS service endpoints will be referenced via the online metadata page located athttps://geodata.state.gov

This is a beta release designed for testing and evaluation. Given the iterative nature of this effort, users should expect that subsequent releases will have modifications, including international land boundary alignment, shoreline resolution, attribute structure, and release formats.

The polygons are not a standalone dataset. They must be used with the matching LSIB overlay and a shoreline dataset. This polygon data set alone should not be relied upon as a representation of the views of the United States regarding sovereignty or international boundaries. The source LSIB line dataset is available for download on geodata.state.gov, data.gov, and geoplatform.gov. The inclusion of a shoreline file is intended only for cartographic purposes.


Cartographic Visualization

The proper use of the World Polygon dataset in cartographic products requires the layering of the LSIB lines on top of the polygons along with the corresponding shoreline dataset. The edges of the polygon must be turned off. When combined with the polygon dataset, the LSIB lines must be symbolized with a visual hierarchy corresponding with the “Rank” field and labeled according to the “Label” field. The polygons should not have an outline or stroke added that conflicts with the LSIB line depiction.

When using colors to separate geographic entities, use the “MapTint_2” or “Map_Sov_Tint_3” fields. These fields are populated with the GENC two- and three-character codes corresponding with the country or area that should be used to show sovereignty for cartographic purposes. In other words, these attributes link dependencies (e.g., Greenland) with the parent country (e.g., Denmark). Similar linkages are encoded in the WP_ID and WP_PAR_ID fields.

The “Label” field contains suggested labels for polygon entities. Not all polygons have required labels, and some labels are not suitable for use at all scales. The “Entity” field is not appropriate for labeling as that field is only designed for data management purposes and provides a readable name corresponding to a “WP_ID” entry. Labels derived from this field require additional manual editing. Any labels applied on cartographic products should be reviewed for appropriate use of diacritics, case, and should reflect general USG standards for the labeling of dependencies, areas of special sovereignty, and administrative units.

The polygon layers contain the Caspian Sea as a data artifact. The Caspian Sea does not need to be cartographically represented.

 

Additional information
Specific cartographic information can be found in Guidance Bulletins published by the Office of the Geographer and Global Issues (https://hiu.state.gov/data/cartographic_guidance_bulletins/).
For U.S. Government and military users, additional boundaries information and analysis can be accessed through the Boundaries and Sovereignty Encyclopedia (BASE) web application maintained by the Office of the Geographer and Global Issues. BASE can be accessed on the internet athttps://statetoday.net/base. Access requires a username and password which can be requested through the site for users with a .gov or .mil email address.

Statistics are broken down by Gender, Age, Hague Convention Status, and Country, and can be filtered by Hague Convention Status. Adoptions can also be viewed by Country, State, Year, and Visa Type. 

Data is received from CA/OCS (Overseas Citizens Services) in August for the previous fiscal year and is then appended to the current datasets and application. Questions about data can be directed to OCS. 

This data was last updated in 2000.
